scenes.title: dbt refs & the DAG
scenes.narration: In this lesson we see how the ref function connects models together and how dbt turns those connections into an execution graph.

scenes.title: Why ref beats a hard-coded name
bullets: It resolves to the correct schema per environment
It registers a dependency between models
It lets dbt choose the right build order
scenes.narration: The ref function is how one model reads from another. Unlike a hard-coded table name, ref automatically resolves to the correct schema for your current environment, whether that is development or production. More importantly, every ref registers a dependency, and it is those recorded dependencies that let dbt figure out the correct order in which to build your models.

scenes.title: ref in action
scenes.code:
-- models/marts/fct_orders.sql
select
    o.order_id,
    o.order_date,
    c.customer_name
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
join {{ ref('stg_customers') }} c
    on o.customer_id = c.customer_id
scenes.narration: This fact model references two staging models by name using ref. When dbt parses the project, it reads these ref calls and records that fct_orders depends on both stg_orders and stg_customers. Because the dependency is expressed in code rather than configured by hand, the graph can never drift out of sync with the actual SQL.

scenes.title: How dbt builds the DAG
steps: Parse every ref and source call
scenes.narration: From all those ref and source calls dbt assembles a directed acyclic graph, or DAG, where each node is a model and each edge is a dependency. dbt then walks this graph, guaranteeing that a model is only built after everything it depends on has already been built. Independent branches of the graph can even be built in parallel to save time.

scenes.title: The payoff of the DAG
bullets: Correct ordering with zero manual scheduling
Node selection to run just part of the graph
scenes.narration: This graph is the quiet engine behind dbt's best features. You never manually order your runs because the DAG does it for you, you can select just one branch of the graph to rebuild during development, and the same graph powers the interactive lineage diagrams in dbt's documentation site.

scenes.text: Never query another model by its raw table name; always use ref() so dbt can order builds and track lineage correctly.
scenes.narration: The golden rule is to never query another model by its raw table name and instead always reach for the ref function, because that single habit is what lets dbt order your builds correctly and keep lineage accurate.
